What makes probiotics and viruses so amazing?

Among the tiny microbes you can't see with your eyes, there are good-for-you probiotics and there are viruses to watch out for. The invisible world is truly fascinating.

content.text:
Nature and science facts about probiotics and viruses

Probiotics are good microbes that live in our gut, help digestion, and hold back harmful bacteria. About 70% of our body's immune cells are gathered in the gut, so a healthy gut also helps our immune system. A virus is much smaller than a probiotic and can't live on its own — it has to get inside another cell to multiply. The best ways to prevent it are vaccination and washing your hands with soap for at least 30 seconds.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Why are probiotics good for you?
A. They live in the gut, help digestion, and hold back harmful bacteria. About 70% of our immune cells are in the gut, so they also help our immune system.

Q. How do you prevent viruses?
A. Vaccination and washing your hands with soap for at least 30 seconds are the most effective.

Q. How can we explore this at home?
A. Talk about the "good bacteria" with yogurt and kimchi, and make washing hands for 30 seconds a habit with a song.
